//sanitize-html: TASK-350. EXACT, and the reason for the exactness CHANGED — read this before
relaxing it to a caret.
2.17.6 is a security release: GHSA-jxwj-j7wr-gfrw, an allowedTags bypass via
raw-text elements (`textarea`, `xmp`). Reproduced against 2.17.5 in this repo:
with `textarea`/`xmp` in allowedTags, all four published payloads emit a live
``. Our two policies (sanitizeRichText, sanitizeSvg)
allow neither tag, so a 103-case sweep of the whole class found 0 escapes on
2.17.5 — we were never exploitable. But that safety was a property of our
allow-lists, not of the library, and one `allowedTags` edit away from being
false. Hence the upgrade. The regression tests in sanitize-rich-text.spec.ts
and sanitize-svg.spec.ts now hold that line directly.
WHY 2.17.5 WAS PINNED (TASK-343): 2.17.6 moved to htmlparser2 ^12, which is
ESM-only (`type: module`, no `require` condition), and Jest's CJS sandbox
cannot load it — 21 store-api suites failed to even start. That is now fixed
in the three jest configs (this file, test/jest-e2e.json, test/jest-int.json)
with a transformIgnorePatterns carve-out; see the comment there. So the
ORIGINAL reason for the pin is gone.
WHY IT IS STILL EXACT: 2.17.6 declares `engines: node >=22.12.0`, because it
relies on Node's `require(esm)`. store-api's runtime image is `node:20-alpine`
(Node 20.20.2). That combination WORKS — `require(esm)` was backported to
20.19.0, verified by loading the package under a real Node 20.19.5 — and npm
has no engine-strict here, so `npm ci` only warns. But we are outside the
range upstream supports, so the next minor is free to use a Node 22 API and
would break the API container silently on a version bump nobody reviewed. An
exact pin makes that impossible.
TO UNPIN BACK TO A CARET: move store-api off Node 20 first (it went EOL
2026-04-30 anyway) — apps/store-api/Dockerfile and the node-version: 20 jobs
in .github/workflows/ci.yml. Then `^2.17.6` is safe again.
── THE JEST CARVE-OUT THAT MAKES 2.17.6 LOADABLE ──────────────────────────
Explained here rather than beside the config because Jest VALIDATES its own
option names and prints a full 'Unknown option' warning, comment body and
all, on every single run. The `jest` key below and the two standalone
configs (test/jest-e2e.json, test/jest-int.json) therefore carry the
carve-out verbatim and no commentary — all three must stay identical.
htmlparser2 12 is ESM-only (`type: module`, no `require` condition in
exports), as are its own deps domhandler@6, domutils@4, domelementtype@3,
entities@8 and dom-serializer@3. Node >= 20.19 loads those from CJS via
`require(esm)`; Jest's CJS module registry does not implement `require(esm)`
at all, so without the carve-out 21 suites die with 'Cannot use import
statement outside a module'.
The carve-out names the WHOLE ESM chain, not just sanitize-html, and that is
the load-bearing detail. The one-name idiom `/node_modules/(?!sanitize-html/)`
genuinely does fail on a nested copy — the path holds `/node_modules/` twice
and the regex matches at the second one, where the lookahead no longer
applies. Listing every package in the chain removes that second position: at
`.../sanitize-html/node_modules/htmlparser2/...` BOTH occurrences are followed
by an allow-listed name, so neither matches and the file is transformed.
An earlier revision anchored the pattern (`^(?!.*/node_modules/sanitize-html/
node_modules/).*/node_modules/`) instead. That worked, but only while
htmlparser2@12 stays NESTED — and it is nested purely because htmlparser2@10
happens to hold the root for other dependents. The day that root consumer goes
away or bumps to 12, npm hoists 12 to the root, the anchored path stops
matching, and 21 suites die with an error that points at Jest rather than at
the hoist that caused it. The name-based form is position-independent: nested
or hoisted, both resolve the same. Verified against both path shapes.
Write POSIX slashes only: Jest passes these through replacePathSepForRegex,
which rewrites `/` to `\\` on Windows.
The matching `transform` entry must come FIRST (Jest takes the first matching
key) and must force `module: commonjs`. The default transform uses
tsconfig.spec.json, whose `module: node16` would honour those packages' own
`type: module` and re-emit ESM — leaving us exactly where we started. None of
them use `import.meta` or top-level await, so a plain downlevel is enough.
REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: `overrides: { sanitize-html: { htmlparser2: ^10.1.0 } }`
keeps the whole tree CJS and needs no Jest change at all, and it was verified
to close all four GHSA payloads (2.17.6's own unconditional escaping does the
work). It is still wrong: the advisory's other half is htmlparser2 12 being
namespace-aware, and the last two sanitize-html security releases were BOTH
driven by parser bugs (8→10 in 2.17.2, 10→12 in 2.17.6). Holding a sanitizer's
parser back at the version just declared insufficient, to avoid a test-config
change, trades the wrong thing.
